Subject: Quick recap + recommended models / next steps (redwood-verified benchmarks attached)

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can run the evals you asked for: 

Recap:
- Goals: customer support triage (classification + short answer) and conversational summarization for high-volume support queues (~200 tps peak).
- Data profile: 2–4 turn conversations, average request size ~600 tokens, critical P95 latency target ~200ms for short responses.
- Success criteria: >= 92% classification accuracy on your intent set; p95 latency <= 220ms in canary; cost target roughly <= $0.006/token (we'll iterate).

Recommended starting models (based on initial match to accuracy/latency/cost tradeoffs):
- rw-large-v1 (higher quality, CPU/GPU baseline) — good for the summarization job
- rw-quant-8k-v2 (8-bit quantized) — strong throughput, lower unit cost, slightly higher p95 latency variance
- rw-7b-condensed (low-latency variant) — good balance for the 200 TPS target on Dedicated pools

I've attached a short benchmark_summary.csv with our baseline TPS and latency percentiles from a comparable customer run, and a shorter MSLA + redlines stub for procurement. Benchmark links and our Redwood-verified profiles: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/ftco-2026-06 (shared below). The Drive folder has the prompt set we propose to use for initial quality checks.

Next steps:
1) If you confirm the models above, we'll schedule a 2-hour canary run against a sample of your prompt set (we'll use the Drive link).
2) Marissa (cc) will scope test infra (GPU type / Dedicated vs Hosted) and provide estimated costs.
3) Procurement — if you want, loop in your procurement contact and we can surface the MSLA redlines.

Proposed times for canary: Thu 2026-06-18 09:00 PT or Fri 2026-06-19 10:00 PT. Does either work?

Attachments: benchmark_summary.csv (baseline metrics), FinTechCo_MSLA_redlines.pdf (redlines only)

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick sync if useful.

—Alex

Liam —

Great — thanks. Short answers + links below. I'll also attach a condensed Redwood-verified performance profile table and the prompt set link in Drive.

Summary of expected performance (tested by Redwood on standard 80GB A100 equivalent and on Dedicated 8xA100 pools):
- rw-large-v1:
  - Hosted (c5e+infer): p50 ~ 45ms, p95 ~ 210ms, p99 ~ 420ms; sustained ~45 TPS per GPU; best for higher-quality summarization but higher cost per token.
  - Dedicated (8xA100 pool, batching tuned): aggregate ~360 TPS (continuous), p95 ~ 180–230ms depending on sequence length; good canary target for quality checks.
- rw-quant-8k-v2:
  - Hosted: p50 ~ 55ms, p95 ~ 280ms, p99 ~ 520ms; individual GPU throughput higher (~60 TPS) but quantized variance on p95 is larger.
  - Dedicated (8xA100): aggregate ~480 TPS; p95 ~ 210–260ms depending on KV cache hit rates.
- rw-7b-condensed:
  - Hosted: p50 ~ 28ms, p95 ~ 150ms, p99 ~ 300ms; good for low-latency short responses.
  - Dedicated: aggregate ~640 TPS; p95 ~ 120–160ms.

Notes/Tradeoffs:
- Sequence length and presence of KV cache have large effects on p95. Our benchmark_summary.csv includes separate rows for avg seq length 600 and 1,200 tokens.
- Quantized models reduce unit cost but can increase p95 variance — recommend testing with your prompt set.
- For the 200 TPS peak and p95 <=220ms target, the pragmatic approach is to run the canary on rw-7b-condensed and rw-large-v1 (sample both quality and latency). rw-7b-condensed should comfortably meet the latency target on Dedicated; rw-large-v1 will validate quality needs.

Benchmark links / artifacts:
- Redwood verified benchmarks: https://redwood.ai/benchmarks/ftco-2026-06 (includes per-GPU and aggregate TPS, p50/p95/p99 tables)
- Drive prompt set: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-model-fit-evals
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/FTCO-2026-06-002

Proposed canary plan (Marissa to coordinate):
- 2-hour run, test both rw-7b-condensed and rw-large-v1 across Hosted and Dedicated dev pool, report p50/p95/p99, throughput, and quality (intent accuracy + summarization ROUGE-like metric)

Marissa / Dylan — can you confirm infra and a run owner? Liam — Thu 6/18 09:00 PT confirmed on our side.

—Alex
Alex Martinez
